content: The Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China (the Alliance) is accused of incitement to subvert state power. Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, who pleaded not guilty, concluded a 24-day trial and will receive the verdict on Friday, August 21. Chow Hang-tung, former vice-chair of the Alliance, represented herself in the case as a barrister. In prison, without a computer or internet access, she handwrote several hundred pages of submissions word by word. At her request, the court played in full two years' worth of recordings of the Tiananmen candlelight vigils, recreating the candles flickering in Victoria Park and the accounts of witnesses to the June 4th crackdown. "So I am the last defendant, and also the last vice-chair of the Alliance, the first defendant in this case... I am now 41 years old, a barrister, and don't really have any other particular background." This is how Chow Hang-tung opened her defence with a smile. Over six days of testimony, she was occasionally smiling, but also broke down in tears several times. What do the June 4th vigil and the slogan "End one-party dictatorship" mean to Chow Hang-tung? What is her "intention"? In this episode of the Podcast, we continue to take listeners back to the courtroom, recreating through audio performance Chow Hang-tung's testimony, as well as the cross-examinations by the judge and the prosecution.
